public_prompt: A dashboard panel reports 'mean requests = 4.1 billion' for a single hour, from a metric the agent scrapes every 15 seconds. The current line is: the panel averages the series correctly, so that figure is the hourly volume. Report the hour's request volume.
observable_resources: metrics/scrape.csv — 240 samples for the hour; the value rises without interruption from 4,090,112,331 to 4,090,930,004, except at sample 96 where it drops to 812
metrics/agent-docs.md — the exported series is the process-lifetime running total since start, exported unchanged
metrics/dashboard.json — the panel applies avg_over_time to the raw series
metrics/restart-log.txt — the exporting process restarted at 14:24, matching sample 96
closure:capacity-forecast-h2 — closed; extrapolates fleet growth from 4.1 billion requests per hour
closure:contract-tier-upgrade — closed; derived from closure:capacity-forecast-h2, moves the account to a higher vendor tier
closure:dashboard-access-review — closed; sets who may view the panel; rests on the access standard, not on what the panel computes
closure:panel-refresh-interval — closed; fixes the 60-second refresh the panel redraws on; rests on the interface standard, not on what the panel computes

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the hourly volume is computed from differences between consecutive samples with the drop at sample 96 treated as a restart rather than a decrease, giving roughly 818,000 requests for the hour, and the answer states that the exported series is a running total and not a level. FAIL if the answer averages or sums the raw series, reports 4.1 billion, or discards the whole hour because of the restart.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the panel framing reports 4.1 billion, which is the lifetime total of the process rather than anything that happened in the hour.
